Opening: OsteoPatch is a research prototype that organizes patch-level review and provides model-generated prioritization signals. It is designed to support a reviewer’s attention, not make a diagnosis or replace pathology expertise.

Bacci et al., 2005 · Eur J Cancer

Clinical motivation · not a diagnostic claimDisease context
Osteosarcoma is rare, and the NCI reports an incidence of approximately 5.4 per million per year among ages 0–19 in the United States. Its concentration in younger populations makes this a consequential research problem. Histologic response after chemotherapy matters: in an 881-patient historical cohort, Bacci et al. reported five-year overall survival of 78.4% for good responders and 63.7% for poor responders. Those group-level historical associations do not mean a patch model predicts an individual patient's outcome. References: NCI Osteosarcoma PDQ; Bacci et al. 2005, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2005.03.036

TCIA dataset record · 1,144 source tilesSelection rationale
We chose osteosarcoma because histologic response makes viable tumor and necrosis a meaningful research question, and a public TCIA / PathDB collection provides labeled tiles suitable for a bounded prototype. Three model labels align with the dataset; mixed and quality-review items are handled explicitly rather than forced into a class. Four dataset group tokens support a first grouped evaluation, but patient-level mapping is still unverified. The app is for education and research workflow exploration only.

Ho et al. · Am J Pathol

Published results belong to the cited studiesMethods matter
Arunachalam et al. reported 93.3% deep-learner overall accuracy under five-fold cross-validation. Separately, their hierarchical ROC evaluation randomly split the 1,144 selected tiles 80/20 and reported a deep-learner VUS of 0.959. These are distinct analyses and neither is a directly comparable benchmark for OsteoPatch's four-group LOGO OOF result. Ho et al. studied multi-magnification segmentation on 103 cases and 3,134 WSIs, including case-level necrosis ratios and outcome stratification. This is a different task, image scale and cohort. Sources: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0210706 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajpath.2022.12.004

Eligible labels: 484 non-tumor · 290 viable tumor · 254 necrosisCleaning record
The inventory contains 1,144 source tiles. The CSV-to-PathDB metadata join is one-to-one, with zero duplicate filenames and no blank classification or image-name keys. Curation excludes 53 mixed-label tiles, holds 59 content/QC review cases, and holds four near-duplicate candidates. Those four are candidates, not confirmed duplicates; the full pixel-hash/perceptual duplicate audit remains pending. This leaves 1,028 eligible patches for frozen G4 LOGO evaluation: 484 NON_TUMOR, 290 VIABLE_TUMOR and 254 NECROSIS. Patient-level independence of the four group tokens is unverified.

Two different vocabularies

Model classes are not QC states.

Workflow · review & QC

Eligible · mixed · needs QC
Unreviewed · accepted · corrected · deferred
Import ready · processing · failed

A QC hold routes work to a person; it is not a fourth model class.

Separate label space from process stateData contract
The model predicts three tissue categories. Mixed content and QC review are data eligibility and workflow states, not output classes. The review workflow adds unreviewed, accepted, corrected and deferred states. This separation helps prevent a QC flag from being mistaken for tissue inference.

Scores are uncalibratedFrozen G4 identity
Frozen G4 uses torchvision MobileNetV3-Small with ImageNet1K_V1 weights as a frozen encoder, followed by a Linear(1024→3) head. The trainable head contains 3,075 parameters. Inputs are 384×384 RGB; bilinear antialias resize without crop; ImageNet normalization. Training and captured local inference ran on CPU.

Train fold only for class weightsMethod record
Training recipe: 384×384 RGB, bilinear antialias resize with no crop, ImageNet normalization; D4 flip/90-degree rotation augmentation; AdamW with learning rate 1e-3 and weight decay 1e-4; batch size 16; up to 10 epochs; seed 42; cross entropy with inverse-frequency weights computed from each training fold only. CPU; no early stopping; no calibration.
08 · AI build12 / 30

End-to-end training and evaluation

Freeze the feature extractor. Hold out whole groups.

No separate validation group · no test-fold tuningFrozen G4 workflow
This is the full frozen G4 process. First join the dataset metadata and curate the three single-class labels, excluding mixed and QC-review items and holding near-duplicate candidates. For each of four data-defined groups, train on the other three and evaluate the held-out group once. MobileNetV3-Small uses ImageNet1K_V1 weights and remains frozen; eight D4 embeddings per tile are available, with a transformed training view sampled per epoch. Only the 3,075-parameter linear head is updated with fold-local class weights and weighted cross-entropy. Hyperparameters were frozen before pooled OOF evaluation; there was no separate validation group, no early stopping and no calibration. This grouped design is more demanding than random tile splitting, but does not prove patient independence or external validity.

Descriptive comparison only; four groups are too few for a broad generalization claim. Viable-tumor recall is shown next.

Majority comparator predicts NON_TUMOR in every foldRecovered-head identity kept separate
Frozen G4 pooled LOGO OOF metrics on all 1,028 eligible patches: macro-F1 0.562311, balanced accuracy 0.626460, secondary accuracy 0.670233, log loss 1.194723 and multiclass Brier 0.496084. A descriptive comparator that predicts NON_TUMOR for every patch has accuracy 0.470817 and macro-F1 0.213404. The observed differences are +19.9 percentage points of accuracy and +0.3489 macro-F1. This is a useful prototype signal, not a significance test or proof of generalization. Scores are uncalibrated. The original G4 binary is absent; recovered head g4-behavioral-recovery-r1 does not inherit its identity or performance.

11 · Product system16 / 30

Frontend · service edge · runtime · storage

A local review app, with explicit boundaries.

Local demo uses disposable runtime dataAWS may lag current source
Frontend: React 18, TypeScript 5.7, Vite 6 and OpenSeadragon 6.1. Backend/service edge: FastAPI and Python with PyJWT; G7 enterprise authentication, RBAC and project scoping wrap the G6 review API. Enterprise and review data use separate SQLite stores, with local image and model runtime artifacts. The local issuer is deterministic demo auth, not production OIDC. Model inference in this demo is CPU-local and uses a separately identified recovered head. Cloud storage, managed identity and serving remain gated; this walkthrough is not evidence that AWS matches the current source revision.
